title: THESIS-MoE: Trainable Hierarchical Extraction and SteerIng of Sycophancy in Mixture-of-Experts
abstract: arXiv:2608.15687v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Sycophancy, the tendency of a language model to change its answer to match a user's stated belief, is a common alignment failure. Existing activation steering methods typically apply a single contrastive direction uniformly throughout the model, which is an unconditional intervention that alters activations even when no sycophantic behavior is present, trading knowledge retention for behavioral correction. In Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, prior work further suggests that behavior is encoded within expert computations rather than routing decisions alone, making precise behavioral steering particularly challenging. In this work, we introduce a shared contrastive signal, built from matched prompts with and without a stated belief, that identifies where sycophancy lives across the MoE hierarchy and drives interventions that act only where the behavior is present. translated_title: THESIS-MoE：混合专家模型中可训练的分层提取与可控谄媚行为引导
translated_abstract: 谄媚行为，即语言模型改变其回答以迎合用户陈述的信念的倾向，是一种常见的对齐失败。现有的激活引导方法通常在整个模型中统一应用单一的对比方向，这是一种无条件的干预，即使在不存在谄媚行为时也会改变激活，从而以知识保留为代价换取行为纠正。在混合专家（MoE）模型中，先前的研究进一步表明，行为编码在专家计算中，而非仅存在于路由决策中，这使得精确的行为引导尤其具有挑战性。在本工作中，我们引入了一种共享的对比信号，该信号基于带有和不带有陈述信念的匹配提示构建，用于识别谄媚行为在MoE层级中的分布位置，并驱动仅在行为存在处起作用的干预。我们将定位问题形式化为对MoE粒度阶梯的因果搜索。
tldr: 本文提出了一种基于共享对比信号的分层定位方法，仅在谄媚行为存在处进行干预，从而在MoE模型中实现更精确的行为引导，同时减少知识损失。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a hierarchical localization method using shared contrastive signals to intervene only where sycophancy occurs in MoE models, enabling precise behavior steering with reduced knowledge loss.
